subfamily: whiskey highball with a split, sparkling lengthener (cider), after the Codex orthodoxy (p. 201) and the Aperol Spritz's split mixer (p. 202)
glass: tall highball glass (about 350 ml), filled with ice
version: v1.2 (Tomás, round 6, 2026-10-01). The drink is unchanged from v1; the 40% is now marked unsourced. Don Lee's Benton's Old-Fashioned base, as his recipe is printed in A Proper Drink (pp. 275-276: Benton's-washed Four Roses bourbon, Grade B maple, Angostura, orange zest), taken out of the Old-Fashioned and lengthened with dry sparkling cider (Wren r3: the drink walks). Bourbon cut from 60 to 45 ml for the highball's strength band. Spark: the Flavor Matrix's pome-fruit wheel puts pork, bourbon and maple syrup together (pdf 197). Cider 7% or under (sweep). Bottle printed as 'Four Roses bourbon'; its 40% is unsourced (only 'Yellow Label' is on record, Lee in PUNCH, F21; no page gives the proof, Hester r5). Contains spice: the black pepper in the Benton's cure (Hester F26), ruled heat on the safe side (Tomás r4; Wren r4 accepts). Pork fat: no veto, but said in the drink text.
